LHX.sentence: L3Harris has dropped to fresh lows and is now down about a third from its high, but nothing has changed about the business — defense spending is steady, and this is just the smallest of the big military contractors getting beaten up more than the others.

ASML.sentence: ASML has cooled off a touch this week, which is fine — it's still the only company in the world that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, and the stock had simply gotten expensive.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a steady stretch, and unusually the market is pricing it no richer than its lesser rivals even though it's the best operator in the industrial gas business.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has gone sideways while similar tech names rallied, so it's lagging its peers for the moment — but the AI cloud story just keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is flat, but the lab-equipment and biotech funding cycle looks like it's starting to thaw, which could set up better days ahead for their sales.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady and pays a hefty dividend from running its oil and gas pipelines like toll roads — the payout is generous but not quite at the bargain level it sometimes reaches.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced a bit today but is still well off its high, which is unusual for such a steady grower — big companies and the government keep signing on for its AI-automation tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore rose even as copper miners fell, a sign investors are giving credit to its trading arm and its spread across many different metals.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dipped after its update, but the headline price-per-ton weakness is just an accounting quirk of what they happened to sell — the real price they get for crushed stone is still climbing, which is what matters.

KOF.sentence: The Latin American Coca-Cola bottler is having a quiet week, with the Mexican peso — the thing that really moves this one for U.S. investors — sitting right in its normal range.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras had a good day with oil prices sitting high, which is a strong tailwind for this Brazilian oil giant since it makes money well below current prices.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, dropped a few percent, but the stock is priced below what it would cost to rebuild its fleet of ships — a classic bargain level for a boom-and-bust business like this.

MA.sentence: Mastercard ticked up and is now priced no higher than Visa, its twin rival, even though it usually commands a premium — people keep tapping their cards millions of times a day.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company slipped a little and sits well below its high on general nervousness, but hospitals keep doing more procedures on its machines, and each operation sells more supplies.
